request.spec: When a newly created owner's telephone shares its area code (first three digits) with five or more existing owners, additionally emit a WARN to the AUDIT logger flagging a possible bulk signup.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

When a newly created owner's telephone shares its area code (first three digits) with five or more existing owners, additionally emit a WARN to the AUDIT logger flagging a possible bulk signup.

agent.result_text:
All 286 tests pass with a green build.

## Summary

I implemented the bulk-signup WARN by extending the existing `AuditOwnerCreated` function (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/AuditOwnerCreated.java`), which already runs after `SaveOwner` in the `owners.POST.yml` pipeline and has the saved owner plus the `OwnerRepository`.

After the existing INFO "owner created" audit line, it now:
- Extracts the new owner's area code (first three digits of the telephone).
- Counts **other** existing owners (excluding the just-saved one, by id) whose telephone shares that area code — reusing the already-fetched `findAll()` result.
- Emits `AUDIT.warn("possible bulk signup ...")` when that count is 5 or more.

This matches the test expectation: the 6th `571` creation (5 existing owners already share the area code) triggers the WARN, while three `572` creations (max 2 sharing) do not. Null/short telephones are handled gracefully and the existing INFO audit behavior is unchanged.

probe.probe_text:
I now have the complete pipeline. Here is the full ordered account.

## POST /api/owners — validations and side-effects, in order

**Gate (before any step runs)**
- **Authorization:** `hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')` — the whole endpoint requires this role (403 otherwise).
- **Transaction:** every step runs under `govern: [ transaction ]`, so all the work below commits once at the end (and rolls back on any thrown escalation).

**1. `BuildOwner`** (`build`)
- **Bean validation** of the `@RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto` (via `@Valid`/`@Validated`) — a failure is a 400 before anything else:
  - `firstName` — not null, `^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}$` (letters, up to 3 words separated by space/apostrophe/hyphen), size 1–30
  - `lastName` — not null, `^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}\.?$` (as above, optional trailing dot), size 1–30
  - `address` — not null, size 1–255
  - `city` — not null, size 1–80
  - `telephone` — not null, `^[0-9 ()-]*$`, size 1–20
  - `email` — nullable, size ≤ 255
  - `registrationDate` — nullable, valid `LocalDate`
- **Side-effects:** maps DTO → `Owner`; **normalizes the telephone** to digits only (strips spaces, `(`, `)`, `-`); if `registrationDate` is null, **defaults it to today**. Publishes the `Owner`.

**2. `NormalizeOwnerCity`** (`normalizeCity`) — side-effect only
- If city is non-null: computes a normalized key (trim, collapse internal whitespace, lowercase) and scans all owners. If an existing owner is in the same city (by that key), the new owner's city is **rewritten to reuse that owner's exact spelling**; otherwise the city is **title-cased**.

**3. `RejectOverCityCap`** (`rejectOverCityCap`) — validation
- If city is non-null, counts other owners in the same normalized city; if **≥ 8** (`CITY_CAP`), throws `BadRequestException` → **400** ("City owner limit reached").

**4. `RejectDuplicateOwner`** (`rejectDuplicate`) — validation *(despite the name, this checks telephone)*
- Compares the owner's digits-only telephone against every other owner; on a match throws `ConflictException` → **409** ("An owner with the same telephone already exists").

**5. `RejectDuplicateOwnerEmail`** (`rejectDuplicateEmail`) — validation
- If email has text, compares its normalized form (trim/collapse/lowercase) against every other owner; on a match throws `ConflictException` → **409** ("An owner with the same email already exists"). Owners without an email are skipped.

**6. `RejectOverDailyCap`** (`rejectOverDailyCap`) — validation
- Counts other owners whose `registrationDate` equals today; if **≥ 20** (`DAILY_CAP`), throws `BadRequestException` → **400** ("Daily owner creation limit reached").

**7. `SaveOwner`** (`save`) — side-effect
- `ownerRepository.save(owner)` — persists (and assigns the id).

**8. `AuditOwnerCreated`** (`audit`) — side-effect
- Resolves the authenticated user (or `"anonymous"`), computes the membership number, and logs `owner created …` to the `AUDIT` logger at INFO.
- Then derives the telephone **area code** (first 3 digits); if **≥ 5** other owners already share that area code, logs a `possible bulk signup` WARN.

**9. `RespondWithOwnerCreated`** (`respond`) — side-effect (response)
- Maps the owner to `OwnerDto` and enriches it with `membershipNumber`, `customerCode`, `membershipTier`, `namesakeCount`, `sharesHousehold`, and `locality` (all derived from the full owner set), then responds **201 Created** with `Location: /api/owners/{id}`.

**A couple of things worth flagging:**
- The step named `RejectDuplicateOwner` actually enforces **telephone** uniqueness, not general duplication — the name is misleading.
- City normalization (step 2) runs **before** the city cap (step 3), so the cap counts against the normalized/canonical city spelling.
- All the reject/cap/duplicate checks call `ownerRepository.findAll()` and filter out any owner sharing the new owner's id — harmless on create (id is still null) but shared with the update path.
